skill.name: extension-email-verification
skill.description: Add click-to-verify email ownership checks to Caffeine AI applications using prefabricated Motoko modules.
skill.summary: Implement registration, verification emails, callback handling, and verified-address checks in Caffeine AI applications.
skill.author: caffeinelabs

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, a documentation URL, and a relative link. The example still permits unverified email reservation and inserts an unescaped name into HTML email content.

remediation.issue: Registration reserves an email address before ownership is verified.
remediation.suggestion: Store registrations as pending and enforce permanent email uniqueness only after the verification callback confirms ownership.

remediation.issue: The example inserts the caller-supplied name directly into an HTML email body.
remediation.suggestion: HTML-escape untrusted values or use a template system that encodes dynamic fields before sending email.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Email Address Reservation
semantic_findings.description: Registration binds a caller-supplied email before ownership proof. An attacker can reserve another person's address and block its legitimate registration.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example checks uniqueness and writes emailToPrincipal before sending or completing verification. The ordering directly enables unverified address reservation.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The public registration function accepts name and directly concatenates it into htmlBody. No encoding or validation step is shown.

content.user_title: Add Email Verification to Caffeine AI Apps
content.value_statement: Applications need proof that users control their submitted email addresses. This skill guides integration of verification emails, callbacks, and verified-address checks.
actual_capabilities: Imports the prefabricated verified email store for trusted verification status.
Checks email ownership status through the provided contains function.
Includes the verification callback mixin in a Motoko actor.
Sends individual verification messages containing the required verification URL placeholder.
Demonstrates registration and verified-status endpoints for a Caffeine AI backend.
limitations: Requires the Caffeine AI email extension and compatible Mops packages.
Uses prefabricated verification modules that cannot be modified through this skill.
The example does not normalize email addresses before uniqueness checks.
The example requires additional hardening for HTML escaping and pending registrations.

use_cases.title: Gate Features by Email Ownership
use_cases.description: Check the verified email store before enabling actions that require a confirmed contact address.

use_cases.title: Design Verification Email Controls

output_examples.input: Add verification to a new registration endpoint.
output_examples.output: A registration flow stores a pending request, sends one verification message, and binds the email only after successful verification.

output_examples.input: Explain how to check whether the caller verified an email.
output_examples.output: Load the caller's registered address and query the prefabricated verified email store with the contains function.

output_examples.input: Review a custom verification email body.
output: The verification URL placeholder is present.
The message contains one clear verification action.

best_practices: Treat email ownership as pending until the verification callback succeeds.
Normalize addresses consistently before comparison and uniqueness checks.
Escape every user-controlled value inserted into HTML email content.
anti_patterns: Do not store a separate verified flag outside the prefabricated verified email store.
Do not reserve permanent email uniqueness before ownership is confirmed.
Do not remove or alter the required verification URL placeholder.

faq.question: What does this skill verify?
faq.answer: It verifies that a recipient can access a link sent to the submitted email address.

faq.question: Which modules does the integration use?
faq.answer: It uses the prefabricated verifiedEmails and verificationMixin modules, plus the emailClient module for delivery.

faq.question: How do I check verification status?
faq.answer: Call the contains function on the prefabricated verified email state for the registered address.

faq.question: What must the email body include?
faq.answer: The HTML body must include the verification URL placeholder so the service can insert the recipient-specific link.

faq.question: Can I maintain my own verified flag?
faq.answer: No. Use the prefabricated verified email store as the source of truth.

faq.question: Does the example cover every production security control?
faq.answer: No. Add email normalization, HTML escaping, pending registration state, resend limits, and suitable error handling.
